newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt congratulates Arafat, Netanyahu on Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Egypt congratulates Arafat, Netanyahu on Hebron.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak congratulated the Palestinian and Israeli leaders on Wednesday on reaching agreement on Israeli redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron, Egyptian state television said.

Mubarak spoke by telephone with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu soon after the agreement was signed at the Erez crossing between Israel and Gaza early on Wednesday, it said.
"They expressed their appreciation of Egypt's role and of President Mubarak's eagerness to overcome all the obstacles between the two sides throughout the talks," it said.
"President Mubarak expressed his congratulations at the agreement, which reinforces the march of comprehensive and just peace in the region," it added.
Mubarak was active in mediating between the two sides at moments of crisis, helping to bring about a conclusion to the lengthy negotiations.

But his Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said: "The success of the agreement belongs to the two negotiating teams and to the Palestinian delegation in particular. Do not think that we negotiated on the Palestinians' behalf or that we created the progress."

"The Palestinian delegation negotiated well and took a good stand in an attempt to reach the best solution and the best wording. Our role was to support the Palestinian position because there was delay and foot-dragging which was harmful to the peace process," the minister told reporters.
Moussa said the Hebron agreement paved the way to further progress on the Palestinian-Israeli peace track and other areas of the Middle East peace process.

"The agreement is a step in the right direction," he said. "The agreement comes with American and European guarantees the withdrawal process will continue and will take place at the times arranged for it.

Asked whether he shared the pessimism of former Israeli prime minister Yitzhak Shamir who predicted an early death for the deal, Moussa said: "He has always been pessimistic. My pessimism is much less today after the agreement, pending of course the implementation of that agreement".

Mubarak had said he would not meet Netanyahu until he reached agreement with the Palestinians on Hebron. Moussa said a meeting would be "possible of course if the need arises" but said a date had not been set.
